module_title: Sectoral Infrastructure & Welfare Schemes (Income, Health & Housing)
introduction: This level transitions to high-budget sectoral interventions aimed at direct benefit transfers, major universal health coverage networks, and infrastructural access goals launched between 2015 and 2019.

core_concepts.title: PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
- Launch Date: February 24, 2019 (Launched from Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh)
- Core Objective: An income support scheme providing ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments of ₹2,000 directly into the bank accounts of all landholding farmer families across the country.

core_concepts.title: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Implemented via National Health Authority - NHA)
- Launch Date: September 23, 2018 (Launched from Ranchi, Jharkhand)
- Core Objective: The world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme, offering a health cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 12 crore poor and vulnerable families.

core_concepts.title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY - Urban & Gramin)
core_concepts.description:
- PMAY-Urban: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Launched: June 25, 2015)
- PMAY-Gramin: Ministry of Rural Development (Launched: November 20, 2016)
- Core Objective: 'Housing for All' initiative aimed at providing geo-tagged, basic-amenity-equipped pucca houses to eligible beneficiaries in both rural and urban ecosystems.

core_concepts.title: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)
core_concepts.description:
- Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Jal Shakti
- Launch Date: August 15, 2019
- Core Objective: To provide Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to every rural household ('Har Ghar Jal') by ensuring a supply of 55 liters of water per capita per day of prescribed quality.

important_entities.name: PM-KISAN Retrospective Baseline
important_entities.significance: Though officially unveiled in February 2019 just before the general elections, the scheme was operationalized with a retrospective effective date of **December 1, 2018**. Civil Services exams exploit this distinction to construct tricky multi-statement options.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not treat Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a single administrative unit. If an exam option states 'PMAY-Gramin is overseen by the Ministry of Housing', it is a trap. PMAY-G is under the **Ministry of Rural Development**, whereas PMAY-U is under **MoHUA**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Farmers in Gorakhpur, Healing in Ranchi.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Instantly binds PM-KISAN to its launch site in Gorakhpur (UP) and AB-PMJAY to its launch origin in Ranchi (Jharkhand).

exam_strategy_tips: Jal Jeevan Mission is a favorite for data-centric questions. Remember its baseline metrics: **55 liters** per capita per day. Pay attention to statement-based questions swapping this metric with 45 or 65 liters.
